reelection.rule: Rule: end of the current class term in legislators-current.yaml. Class 2 ends 2027-01-03. The November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file does not store the election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 Senate votes, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 29. Nay or No: 3. Not Voting: 8. Of 32 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 32 (100%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 51 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

finance.disclosure_note: Disclosed contributions only; donors behind groups that do not report their own donors are not in this feed.
finance.cycle_rule: Senate filings use the two-year cycle of the next election. the current term ends 2027-01-03, so the preceding November election is 2026.
finance.scope_note: Figures are committee receipts and itemized Schedule A for this two-year cycle only. This is not career fundraising. Schedule E outside spending is not included.
finance.contributor_note: Itemized Schedule A receipts for this principal campaign committee and cycle, grouped by contributor name. Memo lines are omitted so an earmark is not counted twice. Unitemized donations are not in this list. Not every Schedule A row was retrieved, so this ranking uses the largest receipts returned and can miss contributors whose gifts are smaller but add up.
finance.pac_note: Committees and party committees among the itemized contributors, largest amounts first. Up to five. Their donors are Schedule A filings of that committee for the same cycle, disclosed donors only.

running.label: Candidates who filed with the FEC for this seat. Filing is not the same as being on the ballot. Primary results and ballot access are not shown.
running.year_rule: Senate filings use the two-year cycle of the next election. the current term ends 2027-01-03, so the preceding November election is 2026.

donor_industry.caption: From itemized individual contributions over $200 reported to the FEC, grouped by the donor's self-reported employer and occupation. Employer means where the donor works, not that the company gave money; corporations can't give directly to campaigns. Industry groups use simple keyword rules and may misclassify some donors.

stands_for.caption: Grouped by Congress.gov's official policy area. Shows how they voted, not why. Final-passage, amendment, and procedural votes can mean different things; read the note for each.
stands_for.scope: Senate votes 1–262 of the 119th Congress, session 2 (262 votes, January 5, 2026 to November 12, 2026), from the Senate LIS.
stands_for.majority_rule: Party majority = the Yea/Nay side taken by most members of that party who voted Yea or Nay on that roll call, counted from the party code in the roll-call XML (all members, including ones no longer serving). Ties have no majority.
stands_for.factual_flag: Not yet summarized: this line is built only from the official vote question and the bill's official title.

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

posts.text: Veterans Day is sacred in Alaska, the state with more veterans per capita than any other. Today, we take time to recognize and honor the men and women who’ve answered the call to defend our nation and their family members who sacrifice in their own way too. 🇺🇸 https://t.co/r07TtQgE2w

Thank you, @SenRickScott. I appreciate your leadership and efforts to make the most of every remaining day of our Republican majority. We have a lot of work left to do for the American people, and we need to keep delivering. https://t.co/g2CPPXq6aX

Aside from husband and father, the title I’m most proud of is United States Marine. Today, the @USMC—the greatest fighting force in human history—is celebrating 251 years of defending our great nation. 

Wishing all of my fellow Marines a Happy Marine Corps Birthday! Semper Fi. https://t.co/YtalvN69Dw
More details on the USDA Harvest Fuel Relief Program: https://t.co/uzTvIivea6

Alaska fishermen!! My team and I worked to make sure you are eligible for USDA’s new $8 billion Harvest Fuel Relief Program! Please start compiling and submitting reliable data on your vessels’ fuel consumption and costs to HarvestFuel@usda.gov as soon as possible. Fishermen are also encouraged to set up a https://t.co/GuTN68Lm6Q account ahead of the forthcoming application period.

Great to be in Fairbanks celebrating a $16 million Rural Health Transformation Fund award for Fairbanks Memorial Hospital—the largest award in the state and one of the largest in the entire country! This innovative project will strengthen health care, create jobs, and benefit https://t.co/0144f980gi

Great news yesterday at AFN! The Department of Energy announced nearly $50 million for Tribal energy projects across Alaska—part of the largest-ever round of Tribal energy investments in the history of DOE’s Office of Indian Energy.

The high cost of energy is one of the biggest https://t.co/XzaYAmnPxY

@SecDuffy @RepNickBegich @lisamurkowski @GovDunleavy @MatSuBorough @AKRR More details on the announcement 👇
https://t.co/ZieKR7vGgY

I want to thank @SecDuffy for joining us in Palmer for this historic announcement, and I want to commend @RepNickBegich, @lisamurkowski, @GovDunleavy, the @MatSuBorough, the @AKRR, AIDEA, and all the local, state, and federal partners who’ve worked for years to make this project a reality.

Yesterday, we announced a major win for the Mat-Su Borough and all of Alaska: $249 million to finally complete the long-awaited Port MacKenzie Rail Extension! This investment will unlock new opportunities for resource development, create good-paying jobs, strengthen our supply chains, and bolster America's economic and national security.

Great trip to Homer! I was able to see firsthand the virtuous cycle of shipbuilding happening throughout our great state: more Coast Guard and NOAA vessels mean more shipbuilding and more good-paying jobs for Alaskans. Thank you to Eric Engebretsen, head of Bay Weld, and https://t.co/Bu0CrTQR0P

On October 18, 159 years ago, the territory of Alaska was formally transferred to the United States, and the Russian flag was lowered in Sitka. Since then, our state has proven itself to be vitally important to our country with our abundant resources, unrivaled strategic location and, most importantly, the people, including Alaska Natives who have called this land home for millennia. Happy Alaska Day!!

I always try to greet our Honor Flights when they come to DC to visit the memorials built in their honor or when they come back home to Alaska. As Julie and I were heading to Fairbanks this afternoon, we had a great opportunity to greet our heroes on their arrival back home. Take a look at this parade in Ted Stevens airport. Semper Fi!

Alaska is home to some of the best military service members on the planet. And we need to make sure they have the best equipment and resources to accomplish their missions. That’s why we’re undertaking the largest military buildup in Alaska’s history!

I’m going to keep fighting to bring more military assets to Alaska, to strengthen our national security, create good-paying jobs and provide opportunities for our contractors and small businesses. 💪
Thank you, @VP, for the kind words. But the real credit goes to the brave men and women in uniform who keep our country safe. https://t.co/kHRJDh7Fdm
Great meeting with the hardworking employees at ConocoPhillips who help create good paying jobs and strong communities for their fellow Alaskans! https://t.co/CO5F6XxLY7

Alaskans have a right to produce our own energy and grow our economy. That’s why I put forward the Alaska’s Right to Produce Act 2.0 last week—legislation to protect the gains we’ve made in unlocking the ANWR Coastal Plain and NPR-A from a future lock-up, as was done under President Biden and Democratic Senate Leader Chuck Schumer.

Unfortunately, my Democratic colleagues blocked the legislation, which should indicate what they have in mind for our state if they ever control the Senate again. I will always fight for Alaskans’ ability to realize our state’s full potential for the benefit of our hard-working families and communities.

On Saturday in Whittier, Alaskans gathered to commission the USS Ted Stevens—a state-of-the-art Navy warship fittingly named after our tenacious, late great Senator who served his country in so many different ways. Ted Stevens understood, perhaps better than anyone else, how important Alaska is to America’s security. Many of the major accomplishments we’re delivering today, including the largest military build-up in Alaska’s history, were made possible by the groundwork Senator Stevens laid over the course of decades.

To the men and women serving aboard the USS Ted Stevens: you are now the stewards of his legacy of courage, patriotism, and service. May that legacy live on in every mission you undertake.

Lead with courage. ⚓️🇺🇸

I had a great time meeting with the Ketchikan Wellness Coalition earlier this week and was able to congratulate them on receiving Rural Health Transformation Program funding! 

The funding will expand their Malasakit Matters: Filipino Healthy Community Project, to build health knowledge across the Filipino communities of Ketchikan and Prince of Wales. 

This is just one of six programs in Ketchikan to receive Rural Health Transformation funding. I’m looking forward to seeing everything they accomplish!

Big news for Wrangell! The U.S. Department of Commerce is awarding the City and Borough more than $43 million to support three projects: a deep water port and shipyard, a downtown waterfront expansion and marine infrastructure improvements, and a replacement for the Wrangell water flume. 

Together, they'll help establish Wrangell as a modern marine industrial hub serving the Coast Guard and our military, NOAA, and commercial vessels, while attracting local and private investments.

It was great to be with everyone in Wrangell earlier this week for the big announcement. Excited to see work on these projects begin!
#LNGmaxxing https://t.co/DapPEW414Z

It’s been a team effort with Alaskans behind me all the way. The reason we’ve been so relentless on this is because Alaska LNG if by far the most important project for our future. https://t.co/gnroA3Ikpz

Alaska LNG is happening thanks to a $50 billion+ investment from South Korea that we announced today at the @WhiteHouse. This project will deliver low-cost energy for Alaskans for generations and create 10,000+ good-paying jobs. A historic day for our state! https://t.co/XBQ9mmTbDG
💪🪏 https://t.co/gY6eGplv6O

Thank you to Trill Gates and @YourAlaskaLink for coming to DC during a big week that saw my Bycatch Reduction Act and Cold Weather Diesel Reliability Act pass out of their committees with bipartisan support! https://t.co/gIhFPBvtkC

Julie and I were honored to join the Alaskan Federation of Filipino Americans for their 23rd Annual Founders' celebration! This community represents so much of what matters to all of us: faith, hard work, love of family, patriotism, and military service.

The friendship between the United States and the Philippines remains very strong, but the strongest connection is right here in the families, businesses, and churches that call Alaska home. 🇺🇸🇵🇭

After working alongside Alaskans for years, we’re making progress on my Bycatch Reduction Act—the most comprehensive bycatch bill introduced in Congress. It passed out of the Commerce Committee but was blocked by Democrats when I brought it for a vote on the Senate floor. But we aren’t done. We’re going to pass this bill and reduce trawl bycatch!

For more than 30 years, Alaskans have been asking for a life-saving road connecting King Cove to Cold Bay—and we’re closer than ever. 

On my last trip to King Cove, I was honored to be joined by the leaders working to get this project across the finish line, including Mayor Warren Wilson, Commissioner of the Alaska Department of Transportation Ryan Anderson, and Sean McMaster, Administrator of the Federal Highway Administration.

The great people of King Cove have waited way too long. Let’s get this done!

Exciting news for Alaska! The Coast Guard has awarded a $315 million contract for the design and construction of a cutter mooring and new fuel pier at Base Kodiak.

This is great news for our Coast Guard, Alaska’s economy, and the hard-working families of Kodiak. Looking forward to seeing these projects break ground as Kodiak prepares to welcome major Coast Guard assets—including 2 new icebreakers, 2 offshore patrol cutters, and hundreds of new Coasties and their families!

More 👇
https://t.co/Jh1PjyRoIC

Alaska, it's here! FAT BEAR WEEK 2026! 🐻
The brown bears of @KatmaiNPS spent all summer feasting on salmon, and now it's time to crown the most winter-ready bear. Vote at https://t.co/2rcZbDR9xX.
I'm backing our reigning champ, Chunk, for a repeat win. May the fattest bear win! https://t.co/670xfKXKyh

America is an Arctic nation because of Alaska, and Arctic security is critically important to American security. The Trump administration understands this. That is why, working together, we’ve delivered the largest military build-up in Alaska since World War II. Greenland is likewise strategically vital to American and NATO security, as it was throughout the Cold War. 

I applaud @POTUS, @SecRubio, and others on the very important agreement reached today by the U.S., Denmark, and Greenland, which expands our security cooperation, strengthens America’s military access to Greenland, and prevents our adversaries from gaining a foothold in this important territory.  

From expanded basing and access for American forces to the development of the Golden Dome missile defense system, this agreement paves the way for a stronger NATO alliance and a more secure American homeland.

G’mar Tov to Alaska’s “Frozen Chosen” and to the Jewish community around the world observing Yom Kippur, a solemn day of atonement and renewal and the holiest day of the year on the Hebrew calendar. Wishing all those observing an easy fast and all the best in the new year! https://t.co/7js6XwloqR

For years, Obama-era diesel regulations that cause trucks to stop working in extreme cold have put Alaskans in danger. The EPA even criminalized local mechanics who were simply trying to keep drivers safe. I worked with these mechanics to get them presidential pardons, but we must fix the system for good. That is why I introduced the Cold Weather Diesel Reliability Act, which recently passed the EPW committee and is heading to the Senate floor! This bill will finally stop these dangerous, one-size-fits-all policies from being forced on Alaska.

Alaska is the hub of American air combat power for the Arctic and Indo-Pacific. We’re proud of our brave Airmen—Active Duty, Guard, Reserve, and veterans—and their families who stand watch and defend freedom every day. Happy Birthday to the @USAirForce! https://t.co/jSeJetDUY9

The @SenateCommerce Committee passed my Bycatch Reduction Act, with overwhelming support. It’s the most comprehensive bycatch bill ever introduced in the Congress. Written with the input from hundreds of Alaskans, this bill will reduce bycatch, protect our seafloor, and strengthen Alaska’s fisheries.

Now, let’s get it across the finish line!

https://t.co/88bcU2S9fX

It's National Truck Driver Appreciation Week, and here in Alaska, we appreciate our truckers! Nearly all of our communities rely entirely on trucks to get the supplies they need—no truckers, no goods, it's that simple. Behind every delivery is one of the nearly 13,000 people working in Alaska's trucking industry, representing 1 in every 19 workers statewide. To our truck drivers: thank you for keeping our great state moving, mile after mile. 🚛

The @EPWGOP passed my Cold Weather Diesel Reliability Act! My bill ends an EPA compliance trap and prevents the dangerous shutdown of engines in extreme cold temperatures. This is a huge step forward for truckers, farmers, mechanics and operators who keep Alaska and our nation moving.

financial_disclosures.caption: Official House financial disclosure filings from the Clerk of the House. A filing lists assets, income, liabilities, and trades the member reported; it is not proof of a conflict or of wrongdoing. Dollar ranges and asset names are in the PDF. This page links to the Clerk's copies and does not score anyone.
financial_disclosures.note: Senate financial disclosures are filed through efd.senate.gov, a different system from the House Clerk index used here. Senate filings are not listed yet.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
conflicts.method: Each itemized donor dollar is counted once, under the industry of the donor's self-reported employer; an industry counts if at least one LD-2 client in it lobbied on any bill this member sponsored or voted on.
